chart: Naive full fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B in BF16 with stock AdamW, one 3,000-token example per step, no gradient checkpointing, stock loss, default install (no fast linear-attention kernels): the memory bill against the RTX 4090
status: calculated, not measured: the 27B does not fit on the card to measure

lines_bottom_to_top.label: gradients
lines_bottom_to_top.source: one BF16 gradient per weight being trained; exact (measured as one weight-sized copy on the 0.8B in 16-bit)

lines_bottom_to_top.label: optimizer state (AdamW: two numbers per weight)
lines_bottom_to_top.source: AdamW's two moments per weight in BF16; exact (measured as two weight-sized copies on the 0.8B in 16-bit). Stock AdamW also holds a fifth weight-sized temporary copy during the step itself, not drawn

lines_bottom_to_top.label: activations, 3,000 tokens
lines_bottom_to_top.source: counted on the 27B's own shapes: the tensors autograd keeps for the backward pass in one linear-attention layer (2,193.2 MiB) and one full-attention layer (1,214.9 MiB) at 3,000 tokens, default install, run 3's adapter (measure/saved_activations.py, results/saved_activations.json), x 48 and x 16 layers. Validated on the 0.8B: the same count gives 4.59 MiB/token against 4.82 measured on the GPU. Replaces the earlier extrapolation from 0.8-9B (111.2 GiB)

lines_bottom_to_top.label: loss, 3,000 tokens
lines_bottom_to_top.source: the stock loss adds 3.13 to 3.37 MiB per token at the backward peak on every measured Qwen3.5 model (median 3.21; 13.3 bytes x 248,320 vocabulary entries), independent of model size; x 3,000 tokens

note: the five lines added up; in a real run gradients fill as activations are freed, so the true peak is somewhat lower than the sum
